scope: Deterministic ODE traces of the DECLARED ideal equal-K two-route model (common fixed h, common inlet superheat, independent routes). Not CFD, not field, not blind: parameters and the 12 base cases are the inspected development cases of glacier_campaign_20261103/baseline. Purpose: score endpoint classes with the packet scorer and show temporary rewetting versus sustained recovery. Cost: seconds.
heat_port: delivered heat to toe-route ice = rho_i*L*E_toe*A_toe (W), signed, never clipped
time_integration: RK2, dt 900 s (checked against dt 450 s in the run record)
controls: fixed_geometry (gap frozen at its initial value): temporary-rewetting control, outside any win denominator
same-equations evolving-topography comparator: algebraically identical in this ideal model, so equality is expected and is NOT evidence of superiority

predictions_before_run.rule: Because the analytic bound forbids repair (max repair <= 0.0004 m in 21 d vs 0.0611 m required), predicted class for every case is NOT sustained_postpulse_recovery. Cases with pulse multiple 1 are predicted initially_disconnected (toe dry throughout). Cases with multiple >=2 are predicted temporary rewetting (classes temporary_or_incomplete_reconnection or initially_disconnected, never sustained) with the gap at post_end within 0.001 m of the initial gap OR larger.
predictions_before_run.failure_rule: A single case with sustained_postpulse_recovery, or a gap decrease larger than the analytic 21-day bound plus 1e-6 m, falsifies the implementation (not the bound's assumptions) and must be investigated before anything else.
